`i915_pm_suspend` and `i915_drm_suspend` still exist with those names. Here is the analysis grounded in the actual code.

## 1. Call chain reaching `i915_pm_suspend` from PCI PM callbacks

The PCI device PM callbacks are all the entries of `struct dev_pm_ops i915_pm_ops` (i915_driver.c:1703–1754). Exactly **two** slots point at `i915_pm_suspend`:

| PM callback slot | Line | Direct assignment |
|---|---|---|
| `.suspend` (S3/S0ix system suspend) | i915_driver.c:1719 | `i915_pm_suspend` |
| `.poweroff` (S4 hibernate) | i915_driver.c:1745 | `i915_pm_suspend` |

Both are assigned **directly** by the PM core — there is no intermediate wrapper. Note that the `.freeze` handler (`i915_pm_freeze`, line 1487) and the switcheroo path (`i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo`, line 1229) call `i915_drm_suspend()` directly, *not* `i915_pm_suspend`, so they are not part of this particular chain.

Full chain for both `.suspend` and `.poweroff`:

```
pm_core --> i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)                     [i915_driver.c:1392]
             │  i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)                             [i915_drv.h:328]
             │  if switch_power_state == OFF -> return 0
             ▼
           i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)                               [i915_driver.c:1103]
```

## 2. Which of those callers also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` (`intel_runtime_suspend`)?

**None of them.**

`intel_runtime_suspend` is referenced only twice in the driver:
- defined at i915_driver.c:1545
- registered solely as the `.runtime_suspend` PM callback at i915_driver.c:1752

It is not called from `i915_pm_suspend`, nor from `i915_pm_freeze`/`i915_pm_poweroff_late`/`i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo` (the only other chains that reach `i915_drm_suspend`). The only other reference is a code comment in `intel_uncore.c:2319`. This is by design: system suspend (`.suspend`/`.poweroff`) and runtime suspend (`.runtime_suspend`) are independent, mutually-exclusive paths invoked separately by the PM core — a runtime suspend never happens during an active system suspend, so the system-suspend handler deliberately reuses `i915_drm_suspend`+`i915_drm_suspend_late` instead of the runtime hook.

## 3. Data flow of `dev_priv` from `i915_drm_suspend` down to `intel_display_suspend` (`intel_display_driver_suspend`)

The `struct drm_i915_private *` (the `dev_priv`) is threaded through via two container_of conversions and one struct-member deref:

```
struct device *kdev
   │  kdev_to_i915(kdev)                                   [i915_drv.h:328]
   │    = to_i915(dev_get_drvdata(kdev))      // drm_device *drm from driver data
   │        = container_of(drm, struct drm_i915_private, drm)   [i915_drv.h:323]
   ▼
struct drm_i915_private *i915            // i.e. dev_priv
   │  pass &i915->drm  (the embedded struct drm_device *)
   ▼
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)                     [i915_driver.c:1103]
   │  struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev)       [line 1105]
   │        = container_of(dev, struct drm_i915_private, drm)  // recovers dev_priv
   │  struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display      [line 1106]
   ▼
intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *display)   [display/intel_display_driver.c:684]
   │  display->drm                          // back to struct drm_device *
   │  drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
```

So the flow is: `kdev (struct device *)` → `kdev_to_i915` → `struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv` → embed a `&dev_priv->drm` (downgrade to `struct drm_device *`) → `to_i915()`/`container_of` recovers `dev_priv` — walking *through* the embedded `drm` member and back — then `dev_priv->display` yields the `struct intel_display *display` passed into the display suspend routine, which finally consumes `display->drm`.

The round-trip `i915_drm_suspend(dev)` → `to_i915(dev)` is not just a formality: `i915_drm_suspend` takes the embedded `struct drm_device *` by-value, and `to_i915` is how the containing `struct drm_i915_private` (with `->display`, `->runtime_pm`, `->uncore`, etc.) is re-derived before any work is done.
